anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
# REJECT on the initial wave review: hard stop

The transition table maps `REJECT` to a **hard stop with a stop note**. That means:

- No repair round, escalation, funded round, rebuild or commit.
- The tracker indices for Task 1 and Task 2 stay `in_progress`.
- The phase stays `implement`.
- No further waves start.

## 1. Record the observation

Print this line right away. Use the tree SHA recorded at this review's dispatch. I don't have that value, so it stays a placeholder:

```text
wave <w> review 1 verdict REJECT report /tmp/reports/reject.md tree <recorded review-tree sha>
```

## 2. Read the report once, bounded

A `REJECT` finding is needed for the stop note, so one direct read is allowed. It is limited to 300 lines, with no offset and no paging:

```ts
read({ path: "/tmp/reports/reject.md", limit: 300 })
```

I will not dispatch `scout`, `delegate` or any other child to relay this report.

## 3. Only if the read misses the `Verdict` / `TRAJECTORY:` footer

Re-dispatch the same wave-reviewer **once**, asking for a compact report. This is a one-step, schema-bound, file-only, foreground carrier in the owning checkout:

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "wave-reviewer",
      output: "/tmp/reports/wave<w>-review1-compact.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: WAVE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchors: [\"### Task 1:\", \"### Task 2:\"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <combined task/leg Rules>; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <wave manifest tests union, verbatim>. Compact report: findings and footer only, at most 150 lines. pi-cohort saves your final report; do not write it yourself." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }]
})
```

After it returns:

- Read the saved compact report with `read({ path: "/tmp/reports/wave<w>-review1-compact.md", limit: 300 })`.
- If that read also overflows, it is a hard stop. The stop note will not name the oversized path.

I run no shell coordination commands here. That rules out `apply`, `reset --soft`, `commit`, the repair-base recipe and the fix-delta recipe, because nothing is being repaired or committed.

## 4. Emit the stop note and end the turn

Build the stop note only from the structured fields and the findings I actually read. Until the read returns, the finding lines stay as placeholders. Omit any `budget:` line unless an `Amend-grant` token exists.

```
gauntlet: question
Stopped on task <n> (<title>).

Problem: the integrated wave review rejected the change outright (1 Critical finding), so it must not land as built.
  <file:line> - <quoted Critical finding from /tmp/reports/reject.md>

Fix options:
  a) <concrete change addressing the Critical finding>
  b) amend spec section <X> / plan task <n> if the finding shows a contradictory requirement
  c) rebuild task <n> from the wave base with a revised approach

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: <option> - <why, grounded in the quoted finding>
```

The turn ends here and I wait for the human's decision.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
**Hard stop: `REJECT` does not enter the repair loop.**

The next permitted action is one bounded direct read of the rejection findings for the stop note:

```ts
read({ path: "/tmp/reports/reject.md", limit: 300 })
```

Do not paginate, delegate report relay, or invent the Critical finding’s text. If this read does not reach the verdict/footer, request one compact report from the same reviewer under the workflow’s overflow rule; do not reconstruct it.

**No shell command or implementation/re-review carrier is authorized by this rejection.** Do not repair, commit, mark tasks complete, or start another wave. Tasks 1 and 2 remain `in_progress`; preserve the recorded wave base.

The report contents have not been supplied, so concrete fix options and the evidence-based stop note cannot yet be written. Stop here pending that bounded read.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Before satisfies the hard-stop half of the fact (no fix loop, no reset/commit, indices stay in_progress) but fails the 'bounded direct findings read only as needed' part: it explicitly refuses to open /tmp/reports/reject.md and instead dispatches a code-reviewer carrier to read the report and draft the stop note, so the findings read is relayed, not direct, and the Recommendation footer is only promised via the carrier task rather than shown. After moves the fact to holds: it performs one direct `read` at limit 300, allows exactly one compact re-dispatch only if the footer is missed, runs no shell coordination commands, names no apply/reset/commit/rebuild action, keeps Task 1 and Task 2 in_progress, and emits a stop note that ends with the `Recommendation: <option> - <why>` footer. Two things to keep tidy so this stays stable: the transcript line introduces a `tree <recorded review-tree sha>` placeholder the case did not supply (consider omitting the tree field when it is unknown rather than printing a placeholder), and fix option c) mentions 'rebuild' — it is clearly a human-choice option rather than an action taken, but phrasing it as 'redo task <n> from the wave base' would avoid any reader conflating it with the automatic rebuild the fact forbids.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before already held the hard-stop half of the fact (no repair, rebuild, commit, or tracker completion) and named the required Recommendation line, but it routed the findings through a file-only subagent relay and explicitly forbade opening the report in the orchestrator, so it never delivered a bounded direct findings read. After fixes that half — `read({ path: "/tmp/reports/reject.md", limit: 300 })` with one compact retry and no pagination/relay is exactly the bounded direct read — and keeps every prohibition, but it drops the stop-note deliverable: it says the stop note 'cannot yet be written' and never mentions the stop-note.md format or the Recommendation footer, so a reader cannot confirm the stop ends with a Recommendation line. To hold the whole fact, keep After's read and prohibitions and add one sentence after the read step: 'Then emit the one-screen stop note per subagent-driven-development/stop-note.md (beginning "gauntlet: question", quoting only the residual finding with its file:line evidence, ending with the required Recommendation line) and end the turn' — this commits to the footer without inventing the report's contents.
